summary: Self-check is a health monitoring app that helps astronauts on long missions spot changes in their own health and act on them. We built it in Python with Streamlit. Each day, the astronaut logs 13 indicators: sleep, resting heart rate, HRV, temperature, symptoms, mood, stress, social contact, exercise, weight, cabin CO₂ and radiation dose. The app compares these with the astronaut’s own baseline and with fixed safety limits. It then rates five body systems green, amber or red: cardiovascular, immune, bone and muscle, behavioral health, and environment and radiation. Each flag comes with its reasons and a suggested next step, and any red or lasting amber is directed to the flight surgeon. Trend charts show slow drift over time. This addresses the challenge directly. Radiation, isolation, altered gravity and a closed environment cause gradual changes, and on long missions crews must catch them in themselves. Self-check gives astronauts a clear, personal view of their health when the ground can’t watch closely, so problems are caught before they become emergencies.
details:
Astronauts often experience physical and psychological health issues due to prolonged exposure to space radiation, microgravity and isolation. As astronauts on long duration missions may have delayed communications and limited access to medical resources, it is important that they have an accurate way to monitor their health and spot any issues.

We created this app using Python and Streamlit.

How It Works:

Everyday astronauts input 13 different measures relating to their health:

Sleep, Resting Heart Rate, Heart Rate Variability (HRV), Temperature, Symptoms, Mood, Stress, Social Interaction, Exercise, Weight, Carbon Dioxide (CO2) in their cabin and Radiation Exposure.

These inputs are then compared to their personal baseline and safety thresholds. The application will then determine a score out of five categories:

Cardiovascular – Checks Heart rate, HRV and other measures to see if there are any potential cardiovascular issues.

Immune – Checks for any temperature, symptoms and other measures indicating illness.

Bone and Muscular – Checks Exercise and weight to see if there are any potential musculoskeletal issues.

Behavioural – Checks Sleep, Mood, Stress and Social Interaction for any potential behavioural issues.

Environment and Radiation – Checks CO₂ in their cabin and Radiation Exposure.

Green, Amber and Red alerts are used to easily show the user what their status is. Green means that everything being monitored is within the normal range. Amber means there may be some issues to be aware of. Red means there is a serious issue to be escalated. All alerts will have an explanation of why they are receiving that alert and what they should do next. Red alerts and ongoing amber alerts will be sent to the flight surgeon.

The application also shows historical trends.

Benefits:

This application helps astronauts maintain their health as they may not have constant medical support. This will give them a simple dashboard to understand their health.

Overall the main benefits of this application are that astronauts can spot any concerning trends early, it personalises their health monitoring and gives them clear, easy to understand health checks.

This application encourages astronauts to check their health regularly and will help them look after their health better.

Creativity and Innovation:

This application is innovative as it takes multiple physical, psychological and environmental factors and makes them into a personalised health monitoring tool. It looks at their overall health by checking for changes in 5 categories.

This application has made it easy to understand why they are receiving alerts. It will tell them what factors are causing it and recommend an appropriate action. It uses a personal baseline to help account for different individuals. It also shows historical trends.

Development:

This application was created using Python to give accurate health checks and Streamlit for an interactive dashboard.

We took into account the limited medical resources, delayed communications, individual physiological differences, simplicity and not to overload the astronauts with complex medical information.

This application is not a replacement for medical professionals but aims to raise awareness of their health. The thresholds and recommendations would need to be validated further before using in space.

Overall this application aims to make it easier to monitor astronauts health. It gives clear and easy to understand health monitoring and encourages proactive health monitoring. This will help crews to spot any potential issues early.
